text: Verdict CONFIRMED on MEDCHEM-01: I re-parsed all eight smiles fields myself. Chem.MolFromSmiles returns None for exactly the four cited (app.js:10, 50, 60, 70) and returns None with sanitize=False as well, confirming these are tokenizer/graph-construction failures, not valence sanitization failures. Applying s/OCH3/OC/ to the curcumin string at app.js:50 yields C21H20O6 with InChIKey VFLDPWHFBUODDF-UHFFFAOYSA-N, whose skeleton block matches PubChem curcumin CID 969516 (VFLDPWHFBUODDF-FCXRPNKRSA-N) exactly. The huperzine A string opens ring-closure label 1 at 'CC1=' and never closes it. app.js:60 and app.js:70 literally contain 'C58H92O27 (Onjisaponin V Core Skeleton)' and 'C36H30O16 (Caffeic Acid Tetramer)'. Every PubChem reference the reviewer states I retrieved independently and all match to the character: huperzine A CID 854026 C15H18N2O 242.32 ZRJBHWIHUMBLCN-YQEJDHNASA-N; curcumin CID 969516 C21H20O6 368.4; salvianolic acid B CID 6451084 C36H30O16 718.6 SNKFFCBZYFGCQN-VWUOOIFGSA-N; onjisaponin V CID 177827987 C82H122O41 1763.8 MYKOTWPDDUNUJG-VNBMPPIYSA-N. I confirmed by grep that app.js:477 is the only consumer of the field: `smiles` appears exactly nine times in the codebase, eight definitions plus one innerHTML interpolation. Correction: Two small factual slips that do not touch the conclusion. (1) The absence-grep is literally false as written: 'canonicalization' is absent but the substring 'canonical' matches app.js:178 ('canonical Wnt/beta-catenin signaling'). The reviewer should scope the grep to library/API tokens rather than claiming zero hits for word stems that occur in prose. (2) 'The app.js string ... has no pyridone ring fusion' is imprecise; the string does encode a C(=O)N-C= lactam fragment. The accurate statement is that ring-closure label 1 is never closed, so the bridged tricyclic framework is never formed and no molecule is produced at all.

text: Verdict CONFIRMED_WITH_CORRECTION on MEDCHEM-02: The identity error is certain and I reproduced every step. The app.js:40 string parses to C15H10O5, MW 270.24, InChIKey SXZJEWVPXPKGJG-UHFFFAOYSA-N. A PubChem InChIKey lookup on that key returns CID 14372623, IUPAC name '6,7,8-trihydroxy-2-phenylchromen-4-one'. Real baicalein by name lookup is CID 5281605, C15H10O5, MW 270.24, FXNFHKRTJBSTCS-UHFFFAOYSA-N, '5,6,7-trihydroxy-2-phenylchromen-4-one'. I also confirmed the reviewer's proposed replacement string parses to FXNFHKRTJBSTCS. An independent 5-hydroxy-4-keto-chromone SMARTS test returns False for the app.js structure and True for real baicalein. This is exactly the silent-failure class the reviewer describes: identical formula, identical mass, different substance. Correction: The mechanistic consequence is stated too absolutely. 6,7,8-trihydroxyflavone retains a pyrogallol A-ring, so it still has an ortho-dihydroxy pair capable of chelating Fe; what it loses is specifically the 5-OH/4-keto bidentate chelate, not all iron chelation. Likewise for GSK-3beta, loss of the C5-OH degrades but does not categorically abolish flavone hinge binding, which is also served by the 4-keto and the 7-OH. Rewrite as 'removes the 5-OH/4-keto motif the stated rationale is written around' rather than 'cannot form that chelate'. Also note 6,7,8-trihydroxyflavone is not a nonsense structure but a real registered compound with its own literature, which the reviewer does correctly flag in the fix.

text: Verdict CONFIRMED_WITH_CORRECTION on MEDCHEM-03: Every headline number reproduces exactly. app.js:20 parses to C38H64O14, MW 744.92, skeleton DYTIXWQVBPQHKX, versus PubChem Rg1 CID 441923 C42H72O14 MW 801.0 skeleton YURJSTAIMNSZAE; a ring-quaternary-carbon-bearing-two-methyls SMARTS returns 0 matches for the app string and 1 for the reference, and methyl counts are 5 versus 8. app.js:30 parses to C18H22O8, MW 366.37, 8 SSSR rings, 1 lactone, 1 ketone, skeleton KRGCYOMVCDUGIP, versus ginkgolide B CID 11973122 C20H24O10 MW 424.4, 6 rings, 3 lactones, 0 ketones, skeleton SQOJOAFXDQDRGF. Both app-string skeletons return PUGREST.NotFound on PubChem, i.e. they correspond to no registered substance. Constitutional comparison after stereo stripping: Rg1 False, ginkgolide B False, asiatic acid True. The internal contradictions are real: app.js:142 states C42H72O14 and app.js:370 states C20H24O10, both correct, both contradicting the SMILES. Rg3 at app.js:266 is C36H62O8 against PubChem CID 9918693 C42H72O13 MW 785.0; presenegenin at app.js:182 and 328 is C30H46O6 against CID 21594224 C30H46O7 MW 518.7. Correction: Three corrections. (1) The anomeric census is garbled. My SMARTS gives 1 O-glycosidic anomeric carbon in the app string versus 2 in real Rg1; real Rg1 has zero C-glycosides, so the reviewer's 'versus 2 and 2 in real Rg1' is wrong. The substantive claim, that the C20 sugar in the app string is attached through a C-C bond rather than a glycosidic oxygen, is correct and is what matters. (2) 'Ginsenoside Rg3 Dammarane Core' arguably names a fragment rather than the intact glycoside, which softens the framing, though C36H62O8 matches neither Rg3 nor its protopanaxadiol aglycone (C30H52O3), so it is wrong under any reading. (3) The reviewer understates the ginkgolide B defect. RDKit ETKDG cannot embed the app.js:30 constitution at all (EmbedMolecule returns -1 after 200 attempts, and ETKDGv3 with random coordinates over 50 conformers did not terminate), while the true ginkgolide B stereoisomer embeds on the first attempt. The app.js ginkgolide B is not merely the wrong molecule; on this evidence its ring fusion appears not to be three-dimensionally realizable at all.

text: Verdict CONFIRMED_WITH_CORRECTION on MEDCHEM-04: The factual core is exact. I extracted all eight smiles fields by regex and confirmed not one contains '@', '/' or backslash. FindPotentialStereo gives, for specified/unspecified: app Rg1 0/22 (reference 21/0), app ginkgolide B 0/12 (reference 11/0), app asiatic acid 0/12 (reference 12/0), app baicalein 0/0, repaired curcumin 0/2. 2^22 = 4194304 and 2^12 = 4096 check out arithmetically. index.html:118 does advertise 'and stereochemistry', so the contradicted-claim element is solid. The InChIKey second-block point is correct and I reproduced it: the flat app asiatic acid gives JXSVIVRDWWRQRT-UHFFFAOYSA-N while PubChem CID 119034 gives JXSVIVRDWWRQRT-UYDOISQJSA-N, identical on the first block. Correction: The stereoisomer arithmetic is inflated in two of three cases. 2^n is an upper bound on graph-level stereoisomers, not a count of chemically realizable diastereomers. I sampled 200 distinct stereoisomers of each app structure and attempted 3D embedding: for asiatic acid 200/200 embedded, so 4096 is essentially right there; for the app ginkgolide B string 0/200 embedded, and since the flat parent itself does not embed, '4,096 stereoisomers' is meaningless for that record. Separately, counting stereoisomers of the app Rg1 string against ginsenoside Rg1 is a category error, because that string is not Rg1's constitution (MEDCHEM-03) - the 4,194,304 figure describes a molecule that is not a ginsenoside at all. The title's 'each saponin/terpenoid record denotes millions of distinct molecules' is true only for the Rg1 record. Finally, the proposed hard gate 'fail the build if any element returns Unspecified' will false-positive on genuine natural products whose configuration is undetermined in the primary literature, and it is largely redundant given the full-InChIKey assertion in step (3).

text: Verdict CONFIRMED on MEDCHEM-05: This is the most consequential finding in the review and it is airtight. I pulled UniProt P05067 and sliced residues 672-713: Abeta1-42 = DAEFRHDSGYEVHHQKLVFFAEDVGSNKGAIIGLMVGGVVIA. Residues 16-35 = KLVFFAEDVGSNKGAIIGLM; residues 16-20 = KLVFF; residues 29-35 = GAIIGLM. app.js:277 reads 'KLVFFAEDVGSNKGAIIGLMGGGSGGSGRLVGHPW' and app.js:129 reads 'KLVFFAEDVGSNKGAIIGLMGGGSGGSGRLVGHPWECDRRACPCYRGFWR'; both open with that 20-mer verbatim, not as a motif-inspired analogue. The surrounding claims are as quoted: app.js:281 'Fibril Blockade: 100%' and 'Seizure Index: 0.01', app.js:282 the disruption mechanism, app.js:279 basal forebrain cholinergic septal nuclei, README:77 'Abeta Disruptor'. index.html:362-363 does pair a one-click 'Copy FASTA Sequence' button with a 'Launch AlphaFold Server' link, and app.js:620 renders the sequence to the user under a FASTA label. The pharmacology sign inversion is correctly diagnosed: appending the GAIIGLM second beta-strand to the KLVFF recognition element restores exactly the self-assembly competence that beta-sheet-breaker design exists to remove. Correction: One embellishment to strike. 'Peptides spanning this region are the standard positive controls for spontaneous fibrillogenesis in ThT assays' is not supported - the conventional ThT positive controls are Abeta1-40/1-42 and Abeta25-35, not Abeta16-35. The claim should be narrowed to what the sequence identity licenses: the construct contains both beta-strands of the cross-beta protofilament core and is therefore aggregation-competent by inspection. Note also that neither the review nor my verification ran an actual aggregation predictor, so 'it is a seed' remains a strong sequence-based inference rather than a computed result; the review's own required fix (TANGO/WALTZ/AGGRESCAN) is the right way to close that gap.

text: Verdict CONFIRMED_WITH_CORRECTION on MEDCHEM-06: I downloaded 1VOT and 4EY7 and measured chain A myself. The three load-bearing numbers reproduce exactly: the Tyr121/Phe330 closest side-chain heavy-atom approach is 5.32 A, huperzine A is enclosed by 26 protein residues within 6 A, and donepezil's maximum intramolecular extent in 4EY7 is 15.48 A. My other distances agree to within ~0.3 A except Ser200-Trp279, where I get 13.69 A against the reviewer's 15.07 A. I added a measurement the reviewer did not make: a Shrake-Rupley SASA calculation gives huperzine A 409.6 A^2 free and 12.8 A^2 in the complex, i.e. 96.9% buried. README:45 states the premise as quoted, the peptides at app.js:153, 195, 247 are 36-41 residues, and app.js:154 does assert simultaneous Torpedo-CAS and human-PAS occupancy. The reviewer is also right that app.js:152 quotes C15H18N2O for a 'Pyridone Core' - I confirmed via PubChem that C15H18N2O is the formula of intact huperzine A (CID 854026), so the record names a minimal fragment and quotes the whole molecule. The conclusion, that a 36-mer polypeptide cannot be conjugated to a warhead buried at the base of the AChE gorge, is correct and robust. Correction: Three reasoning defects that must be fixed before issue. (1) The '~1.9 A free aperture' figure is not a valid aperture measurement. Subtracting two carbon van der Waals radii from a single closest side-chain pair distance does not give the cross-section of a channel bounded by many residues, the closest-approach point need not lie on the gorge axis, and the Tyr121/Phe330 bottleneck is known to breathe. Drop the number; the conclusion does not depend on it. (2) 'Fully buried, with no solvent-exposed face available for a linker' is not literally true - 12.8 A^2 remains exposed. More importantly it proves too much, because a slim tether running up the gorge from a CAS-bound unit is precisely the bivalent idiom the reviewer then recommends. The argument should be framed as 'no polypeptide can traverse this channel', not 'no linker can attach'. (3) The Raves et al. inference is stretched. The abstract (PMID 8989325, https://doi.org/10.1038/nsb0197-57) says the analogue analysis 'shows the importance of individual hydrophobic interactions between HupA and aromatic residues in the active-site gorge' - it does not establish that the pyridone is inseparable. The medicinal-chemistry point stands independently and should be made on its own terms: the pyridone in huperzine A is fused into a bridged tricycle, so an excised 'pyridone core' is not a chemical entity that exists. Finally, the proposed steric gate as worded ('reject designs whose linker must pass through a buried channel') would wrongly reject legitimate gorge-spanning bivalent small molecules; it should test linker width and length against the channel, not the existence of a channel.

text: Verdict CONFIRMED_WITH_CORRECTION on MEDCHEM-07: I recomputed the whole peptide dataset independently. Of 25 sequence fields, exactly 22 are composed of standard residues; the three exceptions are app.js:173 and app.js:371 (the non-standard Asx code 'B') and app.js:381 (the literal placeholder 'His14-Phe174-Linker-Peptide-Conjugate'), and app.js:130 also carries a 'B' in an AF3 candidate the UI offers for submission. Peptide-only masses run 2877-5436 Da, median 4112; adding the declared warhead less water reproduces the reviewer's two maxima to the decimal: 45-mer 5436.15 + salvianolic acid B 718.6 - 18 = 6136.7 (their 6,137) and 47-mer 5340.06 + Rg1 801.0 - 18 = 6123.1 (their 6,123). Maximum net charge is +9, on the 36-mer at app.js:153/247. Seventeen sequences carry two or more cysteines and fourteen carry four or more; the 105 complete pairings of eight cysteines (7x5x3x1) is correct arithmetic. grep -c returns exactly 25 occurrences of 'hERG IC50 > 50' and the string is byte-identical across all of them. The Eisenberg moments reproduce exactly: scaffold 0.615 at +9, LC3 32-mer 0.578 at +7, melittin 0.353 at +5, magainin 2 0.455 at +3. CNS MPO citations verified (PMID 22778837, https://doi.org/10.1021/cn100008c; PMID 26991242, https://doi.org/10.1021/acschemneuro.6b00029), including the 74%/119/108/11,303 figures. Correction: Two methodological corrections. (1) The melittin comparison is method-dependent and flatters the conclusion. Eisenberg hydrophobic moment is conventionally computed over an 11- or 18-residue sliding window, not the whole sequence; melittin's whole-sequence value is depressed by its Pro14 kink, so a windowed calculation narrows the gap substantially. The qualitative placement of a Trp/Leu/Phe-rich +9 36-mer in cationic-amphipathic-lytic space is sound, but the head-to-head numeric ranking against melittin should be reported with the window stated or dropped. (2) The prescribed fix asks for RDKit cLogP/TPSA and a CNS MPO score per candidate; CNS MPO is parameterised on small molecules and is undefined at 3-6 kDa, and RDKit's Crippen logP is far outside its domain for peptides. The honest output is 'this modality is not amenable to CNS MPO', not a computed desirability number. I would also add that hERG-versus-lysis is not the whole story: a 5 kDa polycation with no delivery vehicle has essentially no oral or systemic bioavailability and would be protease-cleared in minutes, which is a more elementary objection than either.

text: Verdict CONFIRMED_WITH_CORRECTION on MEDCHEM-08: The substance is confirmed and the literature is real. I retrieved all four citations from PubMed and every quoted phrase is verbatim from the abstracts: Nelson et al. 2017 (PMID 28074653, https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.jmedchem.6b00975) classifies curcumin as 'both a PAINS ... and an IMPS ... candidate', records '>120 clinical trials', states 'No double-blinded, placebo controlled clinical trial of curcumin has been successful', and concludes it is 'an unstable, reactive, nonbioavailable compound and, therefore, a highly improbable lead'. Baell & Holloway 2010 (PMID 20131845, https://doi.org/10.1021/jm901137j), Irwin et al. 2015 (PMID 26295373, https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.jmedchem.5b01105, including the 5.1% and 0.73% figures), and Nelson et al. 2017 ACS Med Chem Lett (PMID 28523093, https://doi.org/10.1021/acsmedchemlett.7b00139) all check out. Asiatic acid computes to cLogP 5.03 at MW 488.71, exactly as stated. app.js:54 and README:36 do present Keap1 Cys151 alkylation as the therapeutic mechanism, and curcumin is deployed as a warhead at app.js:162, 298 and 338. No interference discussion exists anywhere. Correction: One literal error and one serious defect in the fix. (a) The absence-grep is false as written: 'aggregat' matches 'aggregates' at app.js:334 ('Tau aggregates'). Substantively the absence holds, but the claim should be phrased as 'no interference or aggregation assessment', not 'zero grep hits'. (b) More seriously, the prescribed remedy fails on its own flagship case. I ran RDKit's PAINS_A/B/C FilterCatalog over the parseable set: curcumin returns ZERO PAINS alerts, both for the repaired app.js string and for the PubChem reference isomeric SMILES. The only alert that fires anywhere is catechol_A(92), on both baicalein isomers and on salvianolic acid B; asiatic acid, app Rg1 and app ginkgolide B return nothing. Curcumin's PAINS/IMPS designation in Nelson et al. rests on empirical frequent-hitter behaviour, instability and redox/fluorescence artefacts, not on a Baell substructure match. So the sentence in MEDCHEM-10 that the PAINS catalogue 'catches MEDCHEM-08' is wrong, and a filter-only gate would silently pass the very compound this finding is about. The gate must carry a curated per-compound liability annotation (Michael reactivity, redox cycling, chelation, fluorescence, aggregation, pH 7.4 stability) alongside the substructure filter.

text: Verdict CONFIRMED on MEDCHEM-09: Every residue identity reproduces exactly from the coordinate files. 1VOT chain A: 70 TYR, 72 ASP, 84 TRP, 121 TYR, 130 TYR, 200 SER, 279 TRP, 330 PHE, 331 PHE, 334 TYR, 440 HIS - and critically 286 SER, 341 LYS. 4EY7 chain A: 72 TYR, 74 ASP, 86 TRP, 121 GLY, 124 TYR, 133 TYR, 203 SER, 286 TRP, 330 VAL, 337 TYR, 338 PHE, 341 TYR, 447 HIS - and 84 GLU, 200 PHE, 279 GLN. So 'Phe330, Tyr121' is wrong for human (Val, Gly) and 'Trp286, Tyr341' is wrong for Torpedo (Ser, Lys), exactly as claimed, and no single ortholog satisfies the lists at app.js:154, 248, 288 or README:32. The 'CAS Salt Bridge' error at app.js:12 is real and the file does contradict itself, giving cation-pi correctly at app.js:15 and README:32. Correction: The finding is correct but badly under-scoped, and that is why the severity is too low. The numbering chimera is not an AChE problem; it is systematic across every target in the file, and I found residue claims that are wrong under every convention. Human PAFR (UniProt P25105, 342 aa): residue 14 is ARG not His and lies in the N-terminal tail, not TM1 (TM1 = 17-38); residue 200 is LEU not Tyr; residue 174 is PHE correctly but sits between TM4 (134-155) and TM5 (185-205), not in TM3 (92-113). So app.js:32, app.js:382, README:34 and the placeholder sequence at app.js:381 are wrong on two of three identities and two of three topology labels. Human TrkB (Q16620): Asp298 and Tyr342 are correct in precursor numbering, but Glu319 (=Tyr), Val312 (=Lys) and Leu333 (=Lys) at app.js:144 are wrong, and 'TrkB Tyr515/816' at app.js:24 and index.html:212 is rat numbering (human = Tyr516/Tyr817). Human TrkA (P04629): His312 (=Ser) and Leu331 (=Glu) at app.js:268 are both wrong. TREM2 (Q9NZC2): Arg47 and Asp87 are correct, Lys112 (=Ser) is not. Meanwhile the alpha7 nAChR residues at app.js:196 (Trp149, Tyr188, Tyr195) are all correct - but only under mature-protein numbering after the 22-residue signal peptide, a third convention, while GSK-3beta (Lys85, Asp133, Val135) and Keap1 (Cys151, Tyr334, Arg415, Arg483, Ser602) are all correct under precursor numbering. The file therefore mixes Torpedo/human, rat/human, and precursor/mature conventions across targets. The prescribed fix is right in kind but must be applied to every target, not only AChE.

text: Verdict CONFIRMED_WITH_CORRECTION on MEDCHEM-10: Verified directly. `smiles` occurs nine times in the codebase: the eight definitions at app.js:10-80 and one interpolation at app.js:477 inside a div labelled 'SMILES Formulation'. No cheminformatics library, parser, canonicalizer, identifier, cross-reference or computed descriptor exists anywhere in the four platform files. Every formula, deltaG, Kd and ADMET value is a hand-typed literal. The Bento et al. 2020 reference is real and describes exactly what the reviewer says (PMID 33431044, https://doi.org/10.1186/s13321-020-00456-1: a Checker, a Standardizer and a GetParent component, applied to the ~2 million ChEMBL compounds, available on GitHub and via ChEMBL Beaker). The diagnosis that this single missing layer is the root cause of MEDCHEM-01 through MEDCHEM-04 is correct. Correction: Four corrections to the fix as specified. (1) The absence-grep claim is again literally false - 'canonical' matches app.js:178. (2) Step (5)'s parenthetical 'this catches MEDCHEM-08' is wrong: I ran the RDKit PAINS_A/B/C catalogue and it returns zero alerts for curcumin, the compound MEDCHEM-08 is built around. (3) Step (4) is redundant given the full-InChIKey assertion in step (3) and will false-positive on natural products with genuinely undetermined configuration. (4) The most important omission: the gate as designed validates structures only, and nothing in it would catch a defect in a `sequence` field - which is where the integrity risk (MEDCHEM-05, Abeta 16-35) and the three malformed entries (the non-standard 'B' at app.js:130/173/371 and the placeholder at app.js:381) actually live. A sequence validator (standard-residue check, amyloidogenic-substring screen, charge/hydrophobic-moment flag, disulfide-connectivity requirement) must sit alongside the structure validator or the highest-severity finding in this review remains unguarded after the fix ships.

text: Verdict CONFIRMED on MEDCHEM-11: The conflation is real and the reference data check out. PubChem gives 3,6'-disinapoyl sucrose as C34H42O19, MW 754.7, returning four stereo variants on skeleton FHIJMQWMMZEFBL including CID 131752949 with the exact key cited (FHIJMQWMMZEFBL-KQQUZDAGSA-N); onjisaponin V is CID 177827987, C82H122O41, MW 1763.8; presenegenin is CID 21594224, C30H46O7, MW 518.7 against the C30H46O6 asserted at app.js:182 and app.js:328. app.js:58 does merge the two names into one record and app.js:59 assigns them a single hybrid class. Independent literature support: Wang et al. 2021, BMC Complement Med Ther 21(1):267 (PMID 34696749, https://doi.org/10.1186/s12906-021-03437-5) treats DISS, onjisaponin B and tenuifolin as three distinct constituents of Polygala tenuifolia and attributes the hippocampal neurogenesis effect specifically to DISS. The reviewer's own caution about onjisaponin nomenclature inconsistency is appropriate and well judged. Correction: The finding is understated, which is why the severity is wrong. The record conflates three compounds, not two, and the headline mechanism belongs to none of the two it names. The AMPK-activation / mTOR-inhibition / autophagic-flux mechanism asserted at app.js:64 and README:37 is documented in the primary literature for onjisaponin B, not onjisaponin V and not DISS: Wu et al. 2013, Int J Mol Sci 14(11):22618-41 (PMID 24248062, https://doi.org/10.3390/ijms141122618) screened polygalacic acid, senegenin and onjisaponin B and showed that onjisaponin B specifically induces autophagy via AMPK-mTOR. So the record's name, its class, its mechanism and its aglycone formula each point at a different substance, and the two candidate designs it drives (app.js:181-188 and app.js:327-334) inherit all of it. This is not a MINOR nomenclature slip; it is the same failure mode as MEDCHEM-02 at the level of literature attribution rather than structure.

text: Missed by the primary reviewer: THE FASTA SEQUENCES DO NOT CONTAIN THE WARHEAD, so the platform's central workflow cannot represent its own molecules. Every one of the 25 records is described as natural product + peptide, but the `sequence` field is peptide-only in all 25 cases, and index.html:362-363 offers 'Copy FASTA Sequence' next to 'Launch AlphaFold Server' (app.js:660-671). Even a genuine AlphaFold3 run on these strings would model a bare peptide, not the conjugate described - and arbitrary natural products such as ginsenoside Rg1 or salvianolic acid B cannot be supplied to the public AlphaFold Server as ligands at all, since it accepts only a fixed CCD ligand set. The reviewer correctly says the pLDDT numbers are unsupported but never notices that the sequence the user is invited to submit is a different chemical entity from the drug the page describes.

text: Missed by the primary reviewer: THE CONJUGATION CHEMISTRY IS UNSPECIFIED AND IN SEVERAL CASES INCOHERENT - no attachment atom is named on either partner in any of the 25 records. app.js:182 specifies a '1,2,3-Triazole Linker' (i.e. CuAAC) but neither presenegenin nor the peptide bears an azide or an alkyne; app.js:298 specifies an 'Azide Linker' on curcumin, which has no azide handle and no named attachment site; app.js:152 and app.js:246 specify 'Cys-Lys Amide Coupling' to huperzine A, whose only amine is the bridgehead primary amine that is a principal binding determinant at the CAS, so acylating it is expected to abolish AChE affinity. A synthetic chemist cannot make a single one of these 25 molecules from the information given. This is a more basic objection than MEDCHEM-06's geometry argument and applies to all 25, not just the AChE subset.

text: Missed by the primary reviewer: MICHAEL-ACCEPTOR WARHEADS AND FREE CYSTEINES COEXIST IN THE SAME MOLECULE. I counted 17 of 22 parseable sequences with two or more free cysteines and 14 with four or more. The three curcumin conjugates (app.js:162, 298, 338) place a bis-alpha,beta-unsaturated 1,3-diketone in covalent-bonding distance of those thiols; intramolecular thiol-Michael addition will self-quench the warhead before it ever reaches Keap1. The reviewer flags disulfide scrambling but misses that the interference liability identified in MEDCHEM-08 and the cysteine content identified in MEDCHEM-07 are chemically incompatible with each other in the same construct.

text: Missed by the primary reviewer: README:45's 'MINIMAL NATURAL PRODUCT PHARMACOPHORE WARHEADS' IS CONTRADICTED BY THE WARHEADS ACTUALLY CHOSEN. Ginsenoside Rb1 is 1109.3 Da, Rg1 801.0 Da, Rg3 785.0 Da and salvianolic acid B 718.6 Da (all verified from PubChem this session). Several conjugates are majority natural product by mass - the whole intact saponin is being attached, not a minimal pharmacophore. The reviewer computed the conjugate masses but did not turn them back on the stated method, which is the cleanest single refutation of README:45 and needs no crystallography.

text: Missed by the primary reviewer: THE QUANTITATIVE STRUCTURAL OUTPUTS ARE PROCEDURALLY SYNTHESISED, NOT MERELY UNCOMPUTED - a stronger and more damaging statement than the review makes. app.js:791 generates the 'AlphaFold3 pLDDT Score' as 93 + sin(i*0.4)*4 + (charCode mod 5)*0.5, hard-clamped to a floor of 76 and a ceiling of 98.6 at app.js:792-793, so 'Very High confidence' is guaranteed by construction and can never fail. app.js:850 generates PAE as abs(i-j)*0.4 + (charCode mod 4)*0.3, so the 'domain contact map' is a function of ASCII codes and shows a diagonal band for any input whatsoever. app.js:715 and app.js:977 build the '3D backbone' as a sine helix of radius 6 + (charCode mod 5)*0.8. These are labelled 'REAL FASTA SEQUENCE PARSING & 3D BACKBONE TOPOLOGY GENERATION' (app.js:707) and 'AlphaFold3 Real Sequence-Driven 3D Model' (index.html:371). For the medicinal-chemistry audience the operational consequence should be stated explicitly: any two peptides with the same length and composition produce identical confidence profiles, and no candidate can ever score badly.

text: Missed by the primary reviewer: NO EXPERIMENTAL POTENCY ANCHOR EXISTS FOR ANY OF THE EIGHT NATURAL PRODUCTS. Not one IC50, Ki or EC50 from the primary literature or from ChEMBL appears anywhere in the four files, even though these are among the best-characterised natural products in the cognition literature and huperzine A's sub-100 nM AChE inhibition is the entire reason for its inclusion. Instead every affinity number in the file is a fabricated deltaG/Kd for a conjugate that does not exist. Tabulating baseline warhead potencies from ChEMBL is the first thing a medicinal chemist does before any de novo design, it takes minutes, and its total absence is as diagnostic as the missing structure layer.

text: Missed by the primary reviewer: THE ABSOLUTES ARE A DEFECT CLASS IN THEIR OWN RIGHT AND SHOULD BE CALLED OUT AS ONE. 'Off-target Binding: None' (app.js:209), 'Fibril Blockade: 100%' (281), 'Tolerance Rate: 0.0%' (157), 'Cytokine Storm Risk: 0%' (323), 'BBB Disruption Risk: 0.0%' (375), 'Safety Plasticity Score: 99.5 / 100' (291), 'completely blocks acetylcholine degradation' (252), 'completely halting apoptotic cell death' (272). No in silico method returns a categorical zero, a 100%, or 'None'; these are unfalsifiable by construction. To a reviewer this is the single fastest tell that no computation was performed, and it is more persuasive to a non-specialist reader than any of the structural arguments.

text: Missed by the primary reviewer: THE CURCUMIN EXPOSURE ARGUMENT IS LEFT HALF-FINISHED. app.js:55 has curcumin inserting into Abeta fibril beta-sheets while app.js:54 has it covalently alkylating Keap1 Cys151, and the review cites Nelson et al. for the reactivity but never closes the loop: at the sub-micromolar aqueous solubility and minutes-scale pH 7.4 half-life that paper documents, neither exposure is achievable for free curcumin in brain parenchyma, so the two mechanisms are not merely non-selective, they are mutually unreachable. This also compounds MEDCHEM-07 - a curcumin conjugate inherits both the instability and the impermeability.
